answers.question: Zero camera (/api/v1/image/identify, app.api.image_routes.identify_and_compare) transactions in 30 days?
answers.answer: CONFIRMED as 'zero SAMPLED', with a correction to the wording. The 30-day aggregate of is_transaction:true on python-fastapi lists 22 transaction names and none from app.api.image_routes.*; a targeted query on transaction:*identify_and_compare* OR */api/v1/image/identify* returns no results; a query over ALL spans (transaction or child) whose transaction or span.description contains image_routes / image/identify / identify_products returns no results. Correction: the backend samples traces at 0.1 (sentry_service.py:667) and every count() in the spans dataset is sample-weighted x10 (compare_urls: exactly 1 sampled trace, 19 spans, shows as count()=10; the product_specs 406 reads: 3 raw spans show as count()=30). So 'zero' is zero of a 10 % sample; the tester alone ran at least four camera compares on 2026-10-18 (V01, V04, V06, V07) and P(none of 4 sampled) is about 0.66. The plan must not read it as camera volume or camera health. react-native has zero transactions in 30 days as well (its tracesSampleRate is also 0.1), so no camera wall time exists as a transaction anywhere; the only RN telemetry is 27 info-level comparison_wall_time messages in 14 days (REACT-NATIVE-E), re-counted.

answers.question: On the PINNED supabase-py (postgrest 2.31.0), what does .single() do on zero rows - raise APIError (which code/status) or return None?
answers.answer: It RAISES postgrest.exceptions.APIError; it never returns None and never returns a response with empty data. Pins: requirements.txt:103 postgrest==2.31.0, :156 supabase==2.31.0; the venv has postgrest-2.31.0.dist-info (METADATA Version: 2.31.0). The app uses the SYNC client (database_service.py:22 'from supabase import create_client, Client, ClientOptions'), so client.table() -> SyncRequestBuilder (supabase/_sync/client.py:128), .select() -> SyncSelectRequestBuilder (postgrest/_sync/request_builder.py:300-324), .single() sets Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json and returns SyncSingleRequestBuilder (_sync/request_builder.py:208-215), whose execute() (:109-131) returns SingleAPIResponse only for 200-299 and otherwise parses the body as APIErrorFromJSON and raises APIError(dict) (:128-129), or APIError(generate_default_error_message(r)) when the body is not that JSON shape (:130-131; exceptions.py:58-64 puts r.status_code in code only on that fallback). With the object Accept header PostgREST answers a zero-row select with HTTP 406 - MEASURED in production: the L2 reads GET .../rest/v1/product_specs and GET .../rest/v1/product_reviews appear as http.status_code 406 / span.status invalid_argument (6 sampled spans in 2 text compares on 2026-10-14, 185-467 ms each). The APIError's .code is the PostgREST body code, PGRST116 ('JSON object requested, multiple (or no) rows returned', details 'The result contains 0 rows') - INFERRED from PostgREST's documented contract; the body is not captured by Sentry and this agent has no DB access; the HTTP status 406 is measured, and it is NOT what APIError.code carries when the body parses (exceptions.py:38-43). The 406 is not retried: should_retry retries only GET/HTTP on 503 or 520, MAX_RETRIES 3 (base_request_builder.py:55, 99-104), so a miss is exactly one round trip. Contrast on the same pin: .limit(1).execute() returns APIResponse(data=[]) on a 200 '[]' (SyncQueryRequestBuilder.execute :78-98; APIResponse.from_http_request_response :255-260); the sync select builder's .maybe_single() sets NO Accept header (:217-219, unlike the RPC builder's maybe_single at base_request_builder.py:671-674) and SyncMaybeSingleRequestBuilder.execute() returns None (not a response) on zero rows, SingleAPIResponse(data=row) on one row, and raises APIError code '406' on more than one row (:162-184).

evidence.note: postgrest==2.31.0 (via supabase); supabase==2.31.0
Version: 2.31.0 (installed == pinned)
SyncSelectRequestBuilder.single(): self.request.headers['Accept'] = 'application/vnd.pgrst.object+json'; return SyncSingleRequestBuilder(self.request)

SyncSingleRequestBuilder.execute(): r = send_with_retry(...); if 200 <= r.status_code <= 299: return SingleAPIResponse...; else: json_obj = model_validate_json(APIErrorFromJSON, r.content); raise APIError(dict(json_obj)); except ValidationError: raise APIError(generate_default_error_message(r))
maybe_single() returns SyncMaybeSingleRequestBuilder WITHOUT setting Accept; its execute() returns None when len(parsed.data)==0, SingleAPIResponse when 1, raises APIError code '406' when >1
SyncQueryRequestBuilder.execute() returns APIResponse (data list) on r.is_success; SyncRequestBuilder.select() returns SyncSelectRequestBuilder
MAX_RETRIES = 3; should_retry only for GET/HTTP and status 503 or 520; APIResponse.from_http_request_response parses the JSON array (data=[] on '[]')
APIError(message, code, hint, details) from the body dict; generate_default_error_message uses r.status_code as code only when the body is not the PostgREST error JSON
the RPC builder's single() AND maybe_single() both set the object Accept header - the select builder's maybe_single does not (asymmetry)

answers.question: product_data_service.py:195-220 and :360-390 - does an L2 miss cost a 4xx round trip, and what is the zero-row-safe form on the pinned version? (D1, R-A1(c))
answers.answer: Yes. get_cached_specs (:201-224) and get_cached_reviews (:366-388) run client.table(...).select('specs|reviews, fetched_at').eq('product_key', key).single().execute() inside run_db, wrapped in try/except Exception -> logger.debug('L2 ... miss for {key}: {e}') -> return None. On the pinned library a missing product_key is a PostgREST 406 that raises APIError, so EVERY L2 miss is one wasted round trip (185-467 ms measured, 6 sampled misses in 2 compares) and, with ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD off, it blocks the event loop (db_offload.py:38-43 runs the call inline). A cold compare makes up to four such reads (specs + reviews x 2 products). The 'if not response.data: return None' lines (:214-215, :378-379) are unreachable for a miss on this pin (a hit returns a dict, a miss raises), and the existing tests model the miss as execute() -> MagicMock(data=None) (tests/test_product_data_service.py:47-53, :212-218, fixture :20-32), a shape the pinned library never produces, so those two tests pass for the wrong reason. Zero-row-safe forms on 2.31.0: (a) drop .single() and add .limit(1): execute() returns APIResponse(data=[]) on a miss (HTTP 200) and data=[row] on a hit; the caller reads response.data[0] - the module's own precedent in get_cached_price (:273-281) and auth_service._read_apple_refresh_token (:1070-1094, whose comment states '.single() is not used (it raises on zero rows)'); (b) .maybe_single(): returns None (no response object) on a miss, so the caller must test 'if not response or not response.data' (precedent referral_service.py:88-98); a bare response.data access would AttributeError inside the try and be swallowed as a miss, functionally fine but accidental. Both tables are upserted on product_key (save_specs :229-244 on_conflict='product_key'; save_reviews upsert :392-401), so limit(1)/maybe_single cannot see a second row. Return values are byte-identical in both forms: hit -> the same specs/reviews dict (then the TTL check), miss -> None; both callers (structured_comparison_service.py:6462-6469, review_service.py:689-696) treat None as a miss and a truthy dict as a hit. What changes is only the wire request (Accept header or limit=1 param), the miss status 406 -> 200, and the DEBUG line 'L2 specs miss' no longer firing on a plain miss (LOG_LEVEL default INFO at app/main.py:15, so never emitted in prod).

evidence.note: get_cached_specs: run_db(lambda: client.table('product_specs').select('specs, fetched_at').eq('product_key', product_key).single().execute()); if not response.data: return None; TTL check SPECS_DB_TTL; except Exception -> logger.debug('L2 specs miss ...') -> None

answers.ruling_text: D1 ruling (R-A1(c), the L2 read change) - MEASURED on postgrest 2.31.0 (= the pin) and in production. (1) Facts: `.single().execute()` on the sync client sends `Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json` (postgrest/_sync/request_builder.py:208-215) and PostgREST answers a zero-row key with HTTP 406 (Sentry: 6 sampled `GET /rest/v1/product_specs|product_reviews` 406 / invalid_argument spans in 2 compares on 2026-10-14, 185-467 ms each); SyncSingleRequestBuilder.execute() raises `postgrest.exceptions.APIError` for any non-2xx (:109-131), with `.code` = the body code (PGRST116 by PostgREST's contract; inferred, body not captured) and no retry (base_request_builder.py:99-104 retries only 503/520). product_data_service.get_cached_specs (:201-224) and get_cached_reviews (:366-388) swallow it as a DEBUG 'miss' and return None, so every L2 miss is one wasted blocking round trip (inline under run_db while ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is off, db_offload.py:38-43); up to four per cold compare. The `if not response.data` branch is dead for a miss on this pin. (2) Form: replace `.single()` with `.limit(1)` at :211 and :375 and read `response.data[0]` after the existing `if not response.data: return None` - the module's own get_cached_price shape (:273-281) and the auth_service precedent (:1070-1094). Do NOT use `.maybe_single()`: on the sync select builder it sets no Accept header and returns None instead of a response (:217-219, :162-184), so the caller would have to special-case None; it buys nothing over limit(1) because both tables are upserted on product_key (:242). (3) Classification: UNFLAGGED under R-A1(c). Byte identity holds on every response and stored row: the function's return is the same dict on a hit (then the unchanged TTL check) and None on a miss; both callers (structured_comparison_service.py:6464-6469, review_service.py:691-696) branch only on truthiness; no write path changes. What moves is below the response: the request header/param, the miss status 406 -> 200, and a DEBUG line that LOG_LEVEL=INFO never emits. (4) Pin set the unit must carry: RED at base - a fake sync client whose `.single().execute()` raises `APIError({'message': 'JSON object requested, multiple (or no) rows returned', 'code': 'PGRST116', 'details': 'The result contains 0 rows', 'hint': None})` and whose `.limit(1).execute()` returns `APIResponse(data=[])`; assert the miss returns None WITHOUT the exception path (e.g. `.single` never called, `logger.debug` not called) for both functions. PIN - hit returns the identical dict for a fresh row and None for a stale row through `.limit(1)` (data=[row]); a raising client still returns None (keep tests/test_product_data_service.py:261-272). Fix the unfaithful miss model at tests/test_product_data_service.py:47-53 and :212-218 (`MagicMock(data=None)` -> the real shapes) in the same PR, with the reason in the test docstring. Mutation: reverting one site to `.single()` must redden the RED test for that function. Comm set: tests/test_product_data_service.py, the callers' suites that patch get_cached_specs/get_cached_reviews (test_unified_search.py, test_phase1_includes_reviews.py, test_spec_confidence_cache.py, test_review_source_consult.py, test_m13_33_review_fire_and_forget.py, test_youtube_reviews_race.py, test_s75_fanout_starve.py, test_s77_redis_offloop.py), the nine-digest node tests/test_s75_fanout_identity.py::test_FY25_flag_off_compare_identity_matches_main, plus the source-scanning pins per R-A13. (5) Stated limits: the PostgREST body code is inferred (one owner-run request or a LIVE=1 test would settle it); 37 other `.single()` sites in app/ (auth_service x7, referral_service x13, database_service x5, home_routes x2, auth_routes x2, profile_routes, abuse_detection_service, push_service x2, structured_comparison_service:5636, usage_service:530) have the same 406-on-absence cost where the row can be absent (referral code lookups, push tokens) and are out of D1's scope - record them for a follow-up, do not widen D1.

answers.ruling_text:
Corrected evidence lines for PLAN_S80 (replace the digest wording where it differs):

E1 (camera telemetry): 'Sentry sampled no /api/v1/image/identify (app.api.image_routes.*) transaction in the 30 days to 2026-10-19 and no react-native transaction at all; both SDKs sample traces at 0.1 (sentry_service.py:667; sentry.ts:271-280), and every count() in the spans dataset is sample-weighted x10 (compare_urls: 1 sampled trace reads as 10). Zero sampled is not zero camera compares - the tester alone ran at least four on 2026-10-18 - so camera latency and the ~40 s figures rest on the RN comparison_wall_time messages and the videos, never on backend traces.'

E2 (V02 / FragranceX): 'PYTHON-FASTAPI-1X: 4 events, 2026-10-18T12:50:05.062Z to 12:50:15.402Z, release 683f56c0, client MYEZ 3 iOS, two POST /api/v1/url/compare requests (server spans a16a552b3f867bdf and 9ddb2c20a7900d51) in trace 2e59ae38aca04795883c6c9306de3495, two failed fetches each, all on host www.fragrancex.com.
